title: A Master Class of Institutional Knowledge
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece warns that organizations routinely undervalue tacit institutional knowledge and lose it by default whenever experienced people leave or change roles. The author describes concrete preservation practices adopted by disciplined organizations: documented process maps supplemented by video of real staff explaining their work, and structured cross-training programs. The most distinctive recommendation is asking departing team members to deliver a formal 'Master Class' capturing what they've learned before they exit, turning an otherwise ad hoc departure into a structured knowledge asset for the organization.
points: Organizations often lose critical tacit knowledge — procedures, customer preferences, cultural norms — every time an experienced team member departs, retires, or changes roles.
Best-practice organizations combat this with disciplined process documentation (including video of real people explaining their work) and structured cross-training.
The strongest knowledge-transfer differentiator is how leaders capture information specifically before someone departs, even on short notice.
Asking departing team members to teach a formal 'Master Class' on what they've learned turns an ad hoc exit into a structured, reusable knowledge asset.
quotes: Institutional knowledge is one of the key assets in any organization. Held by leaders and team members across the organization, this collective memory allows the organization to maintain standards, make informed decisions, and reinforce the enterprise culture.
With every team member departure, the organization has the potential to lose some of this institutional memory.
In addition to process maps and outlines, the use of video to capture real people discussing how they execute processes is a best practice.
Asking departing team members to teach a Master Class on what they have learned and how they have gone about their work is a positive experience for everyone.
Institutional knowledge represents the long-term health and currency of an enterprise. Good leaders never take it for granted.
